question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To bring home the bacon

options.text: To bring food for a party
To earn a living or achieve success

explanation: Bring home the bacon = रोज़ी-रोटी कमाना, सफलता हासिल करना। Example: Both parents work to bring home the bacon.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be up in arms

options.text: To prepare for a long journey

explanation: Be up in arms = ग़ुस्से में विरोध करना। Example: Residents were up in arms over the water cut.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To blow the whistle

options.text: To expose a wrongdoing to the authorities
To call for help in a play

explanation: Blow the whistle = गड़बड़ी का भंडाफोड़ करना। Example: A clerk blew the whistle on the scam.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To break the bank

options.text: To cost more than one can afford
To save a lot of money

explanation: Break the bank = बजट से बाहर ख़र्च कराना। Example: A small gift won't break the bank.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To chew the fat

options.text: To have a long, friendly chat

explanation: Chew the fat = गपशप करना। Example: The old friends sat chewing the fat for hours.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To clear the air
explanation: Clear the air = ग़लतफ़हमी दूर करना। Example: A frank talk cleared the air between them.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To cook someone's goose

options.text: To ruin someone's chances or plans
To prepare a feast for someone
To cheat at a card game

explanation: Cook someone's goose = किसी की योजना चौपट कर देना। Example: His late arrival cooked his goose.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To dig one's own grave

options.text: To cause one's own ruin by foolish actions
To work hard in a field

explanation: Dig one's own grave = अपनी ही बर्बादी का रास्ता बनाना। Example: By lying to the court, he dug his own grave.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To fish in troubled waters

options.text: To cross a river with difficulty
To catch fish in a flooded river
To seek personal gain from a confused situation

explanation: Fish in troubled waters = अशांति में अपना फ़ायदा ढूँढना। Example: Brokers fish in troubled waters during a market crash.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To fall flat

options.text: To slip on a smooth floor
To fail to produce the desired effect
To win by a big margin

explanation: Fall flat = उम्मीद के मुताबिक़ असर न करना। Example: His joke fell flat.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To get a raw deal
explanation: Get a raw deal = अन्यायपूर्ण व्यवहार पाना। Example: The workers got a raw deal in the agreement.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To give someone the slip

options.text: To escape from someone who is following you
To give someone a piece of paper
To hand over a note secretly

explanation: Give someone the slip = पीछा करने वाले को चकमा देना। Example: The thief gave the police the slip.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To have the last laugh

options.text: To laugh at one's own joke
To laugh loudly at a funeral
To succeed in the end after being doubted
To tell the final joke at a show

explanation: Have the last laugh = अंत में सफल होकर शक करने वालों को ग़लत साबित करना। Example: The small team had the last laugh by winning the cup.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To lose face

options.text: To be humiliated or lose one's respect

explanation: Lose face = इज़्ज़त गँवाना। Example: The leader lost face after the public blunder.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To miss the boat

options.text: To take a risk and gain

explanation: Miss the boat = सुनहरा मौक़ा गँवा देना। Example: Apply today, or you will miss the boat.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To run out of steam
explanation: Run out of steam = जोश या ताक़त ख़त्म हो जाना। Example: The campaign ran out of steam after a month.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To pull out all the stops

options.text: To make the greatest possible effort
To remove all obstacles on a road

explanation: Pull out all the stops = पूरी ताक़त झोंक देना। Example: The team pulled out all the stops to win the final.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To shoot oneself in the foot

options.text: To injure oneself in a hunt
To harm one's own cause by a foolish act

explanation: Shoot oneself in the foot = अपने पैरों पर कुल्हाड़ी मारना। Example: By insulting the judge, he shot himself in the foot.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To steal the show

options.text: To attract the most attention and praise

explanation: Steal the show = सबसे ज़्यादा तारीफ़ बटोर लेना। Example: The child actor stole the show.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To take the cake

options.text: To bake a cake for a party
To be the most remarkable, often in a negative sense

explanation: Take the cake = सबसे बढ़कर निकलना (अक्सर बुरी बात में)। Example: His excuse really takes the cake.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To throw caution to the winds

options.text: To act in a reckless way
To go out in stormy weather

explanation: Throw caution to the winds = सावधानी ताक पर रख देना। Example: He threw caution to the winds and invested everything.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To work like a Trojan

options.text: To work for a foreign king

explanation: Work like a Trojan = जी-तोड़ मेहनत करना। Example: She worked like a Trojan to finish the project.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be in the red

options.text: To be in debt or to have a negative balance

explanation: In the red = घाटे या क़र्ज़ में होना। Example: The firm has been in the red for two years.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To be at a loose end

options.text: To be busy with many tasks

explanation: At a loose end = ख़ाली बैठे होना। Example: Sunday afternoons find him at a loose end.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: A flash in the pan

options.text: A brief success that is not repeated
A sudden fire in the kitchen

explanation: A flash in the pan = क्षणिक सफलता। Example: His first hit turned out to be a flash in the pan.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To beat a retreat
explanation: Beat a retreat = जल्दी से पीछे हट जाना। Example: The army beat a retreat at dawn.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To hang by a thread

options.text: To be in a very uncertain or dangerous position

explanation: Hang by a thread = बाल बराबर सहारे पर टिका होना। Example: The patient's life hung by a thread.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To jump through hoops

options.text: To go through a long and difficult process to get something

explanation: Jump through hoops = कड़े झंझट से गुज़रना। Example: We had to jump through hoops to get the licence.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To lay one's cards on the table

options.text: To be completely open about one's plans

explanation: Lay one's cards on the table = अपने इरादे साफ़ बता देना। Example: He laid his cards on the table at the meeting.

question: Choose the meaning of the idiom: To play it by ear

options.text: To deal with a situation as it develops, without a fixed plan

explanation: Play it by ear = हालात देखकर तय करना। Example: We have no schedule; let us play it by ear.
